body:
# the contributor audit: independent-axis triangle guards and replication


`candidate 2ab56d1c26a2c4f9`
and `candidate b4250d3425f93191`.
Both complete source files were read, including the all-normal argument and
all-menu quantifiers. This is not a counterexample to OC or to stationarity
under signed convex physical fields.

The unit integer crosspolytope has exactly the listed sampled bases. Its
outer bases are exposed; convex combinations returning to zero stay in T.
Thus the canonical convex hull has exactly the prescribed full fibers.
The pooled covariance factors retain only the actual within-fiber
covariances, as required by this interface.

For every nonzero continuous direction, its maximum triangle vertex has
positive value M and every other vertex has value at least -2M. Each
matching guard therefore has strictly positive margin when sigma<1/3.
Pairing its identical reflected fibers proves the global outside quota
for every base tilt. Independent base coordinates attain the quota in
each canonical direction. This is precisely the independence missing
from the older favorable retargeting construction.

The own-cap angular formula has the correct width factor, displaced-area
average, and monotonicity. The complement formula for two positive
vertex projections is at least one half, including zero projection
limits. The canonical smoothed fraction lies strictly below 16/35 at
w<=1/100. Equality therefore classifies all actual continuous directions,
not merely local stationary directions. Equality in the outside quota
excludes every transition region and every nonmatching guard. Continuity
extends saturation to the guard boundaries. The pure-base caps are
strictly larger. Frozen spanning canonical caps prove unique middle
deepestness, while exposed outer caps bound all other candidates.

Equal direction-class response weights follow from equal actual coareas
and the unique positive dependence. On each guard every menu profile is
at most one third. The own-edge profile is symmetric and monotone toward
the middle; symmetrizing any convex test and applying opposite Chebyshev
proves the exact coefficient 4/9+w/3 without a concentration assumption.
The two end strips have convex-test average at least the full-edge
average. Their paired physical Jensen inequalities yield E>=4L sigma I,
with distinct guard/facet incidences and all extra facets retained.

The resulting universal menu/field upper bound is
1/3+(1/9+w/3)/(1+L) for sigma=1/4. At L=3 it is at most
1303/3600<4/11<1/e. A selected cap's positive affine hinge gives the
matching lower one third. The general three-cap lower bound uses the
finite convex-hull theorem on the actual vectors S_N u, followed by
the same hinge; its attained-interface scope is correct.

These examples have only one deepest source and substantial unused
source parity. In addition, signed affine base fields can distinguish
captured guards from their reflected partners. Their nonnegative
capacity bound must not be promoted to a no-descent claim at a true
body minimum. Optimal is separately recording that signed escape.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
